sentences.text: Anasazisaurus was a saurolophine hadrosaurid ornithopod dinosaur that lived approximately 74 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous.
It is known for a short nasal crest that projected above and between its eyes, featuring a unique bone flange rising from the nasals that folds back under itself.
To date, only a partial skull has been discovered, with a maximum preserved length of approximately 90 centimeters.
According to Gregory S. Paul, the animal was about 7.5 meters long and weighed up to 2500 kilograms.
Its teeth were continually replaced and packed into dental batteries containing hundreds of teeth, with only a few in use at any time.

American paleontologists Adrian Hunt and Spencer G. Lucas named the dinosaur Anasazisaurus in 1993 based on the holotype skull, the only known specimen, which was collected in the late 1970s by a Brigham Young University field party.
As a hadrosaurid, Anasazisaurus was likely a large bipedal or quadrupedal herbivore with a skull capable of a grinding motion analogous to chewing.
It likely fed on vegetation ranging from the ground up to approximately 4 meters high.
The Spanish Wikipedia entry classifies Anasazisaurus within the subfamily Saurolophinae.

Fossils have been found in the Farmington Member of the Kirtland Formation in the San Juan Basin of New Mexico, United States, a formation dated to the late Campanian of the Upper Cretaceous, approximately 74 to 70 million years ago.

It is debated whether Anasazisaurus is a valid genus; some researchers, including Thomas Williamson and Alberto Prieto-Marquez, argue it should be classified as a species of Kritosaurus (Kritosaurus horneri).
